claims.claim_en: Rule: the notion 'مُحْدَث' is construed as being carried on the expression «ذِكْر», and it is also permissible to elevate it to the position of «مِن ذِكْر». Applied to this verse, this concerns the element derived from ذِكْر (i.e. يَذْكُرُ).

claims.claim_en: The source lists multiple permissible grammatical attachments for «مِن ذِكْرٍ»: (1) attached to the following verb (يأْتِيهِم), (2) as an adjective of 'ذِكْر', (3) related to a 'مُحْدَث', or (4) as a circumstantial 'حَال' deriving from a pronoun within a 'مُحْدَث'. By analogy, there are several viable syntactic analyses for the 'ذِكْر' element (i.e. يَذْكُرُهُمْ) in this verse.
